name: What is Mental Wellbeing
what: This subtopic introduces the concept of mental wellbeing as a psychological state involving the ability to think, process information, and regulate emotions. It establishes that wellbeing is multifaceted and can be considered from several perspectives.
why: Without a clear definition of mental wellbeing, it is impossible to measure, track, or support it. Understanding what wellbeing means provides the foundation for everything else in this topic.

items.title: I can define wellbeing and distinguish it from mental wellbeing
items.what: Wellbeing is a state in which an individual is mentally, physically, and socially healthy and secure. Mental wellbeing is more specific and refers to an individual's psychological state, including their ability to think, process information, and regulate emotions.
items.why: Distinguishing between general wellbeing and mental wellbeing allows for precise discussion of psychological health, which is required for exam responses and clinical reasoning.
items.example: A person recovering from a broken leg may have low physical wellbeing but still demonstrate high mental wellbeing by maintaining a positive outlook, staying socially connected, and managing daily tasks effectively.

items.title: I can identify the three main ways of considering mental wellbeing
items.what: Mental wellbeing can be considered through three lenses: levels of functioning, resilience, and social and emotional wellbeing. These are not separate conditions but interconnected aspects of the same overall state.
items.why: The VCE study design requires students to apply all three frameworks to scenarios. Recognising that they are interrelated, not independent, is essential for extended response questions.
items.example: In a VCAA exam scenario, a student who is unable to get out of bed (low functioning), avoids friends after a breakup (low social wellbeing), and feels overwhelmed by minor setbacks (low resilience) can be analysed using all three frameworks simultaneously.

items.title: I can explain how mental wellbeing differs from the absence of mental illness
items.what: Mental wellbeing is not simply the absence of a diagnosed mental health disorder. A person can have a diagnosed mental health condition and still demonstrate meaningful levels of wellbeing if their condition is well-managed and they function effectively.
items.why: This distinction prevents a binary or stigmatising view of mental health and reflects the continuum model used throughout this topic.
items.example: Someone diagnosed with depression who attends therapy, maintains friendships, and holds down a part-time job may be placed toward the higher end of the mental wellbeing continuum, despite having a diagnosis.
